## Toronto Apartment Fit for a Family of 3

A is cheaper on rent, but B is stronger on space, commute convenience, and parking. Given your priorities, **Option B is the better overall choice** if you can keep utilities modest.

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Option | Rent | Size | Baths | Subway Walk | Building | Parking | Utilities | Estimated Monthly Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| A | CAD 2,850 | 38 m² | 1 | 12 min | 1998 | Extra CAD 120 | Included except electricity | **About CAD 2,970 + electricity** |
| B | CAD 3,100 | 52 m² | 2 | 6 min | 2014 | Included | Not included | **About CAD 3,100 + utilities** |

## Best Choice for Your Priorities

### Option B — Recommended Overall
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Commute:** Closer to subway, so it is more likely to stay under your 35-minute downtown target.
- **Family fit:** 52 m² and 2 bathrooms is much better for a family of 3.
- **Quietness:** Newer building often helps, though this is still a building-specific factor.
- **Cost control:** Even with utilities, it should usually stay under your **CAD 3,400/month** cap.

### Option A — Budget-leaning Alternative
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Lower base rent:** Good if you want the lowest fixed monthly lease cost.
- **Trade-offs:** Smaller space, only 1 bathroom, and parking costs extra.
- **Best if:** You expect very low electricity use and do not need much living space.

## Quick Recommendation
- **Choose B** if you value easier commuting, more living space, better family comfort, and included parking.
- **Choose A** only if your top priority is minimizing rent and you are comfortable with tighter space.
